summary.text: This briefing evaluates the combination of Gaussian processes, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, and regression for uncertainty-aware scientific machine learning. By integrating sparse variational Gaussian process inference into the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology, the approach uses inducing points and analytic moment matching to scale regression tasks. This combination addresses the cubic scaling limitations of exact Gaussian process extensions while equipping the interpretable network architecture with probabilistic outputs.

target_user.text: Target users are inferred from patent assignees in corporate and academic sectors working on regression, monitoring, and modeling systems, as well as researchers utilizing scientific machine learning repositories and packages. The target user is unverified.

jtbd.text: Perform uncertainty-aware regression and function approximation in scientific machine learning applications where both accurate continuous predictions and principled epistemic uncertainty quantification are required.

value_prop.text: Standard Kolmogorov-Arnold networks lack probabilistic outputs, and exact Gaussian process extensions scale cubically with dataset size. Integrating sparse variational Gaussian process inference with the Kolmogorov-Arnold topology reduces computational complexity and enables scalable probabilistic regression.

riskiest_assumption.text: The feasibility axis score is 3.0 out of 5.0, making feasibility the riskiest axis. The riskiest assumption is that analytic moment matching and sparse variational inference within the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology can maintain stable training dynamics and well-calibrated epistemic uncertainty without prohibitive approximation errors across high-dimensional regression tasks.

mvp.text: Implement a technical proof of concept by combining existing sparse Gaussian process packages with network training utilities to construct a sparse variational Gaussian process Kolmogorov-Arnold network. Test this MVP on a standard multi-target regression benchmark to evaluate inference runtime and predictive calibration.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of less than 0.05 calibration error on held-out regression benchmarks while maintaining a computational scaling complexity that is quasi-linear relative to sample size.

kill_criteria.text: If the sparse variational Gaussian process approximation degrades predictive accuracy on regression tasks below the baseline multi-layer perceptron or standard Gaussian process by a proposed threshold of more than 15 percent, the approach is killed.
If training complexity exceeds a proposed threshold of $O(N^2)$ scaling with respect to sample size due to edge-wise variational parameter interactions, the combination is deemed infeasible.

open_source.use: Used as a machine learning utility package to support general modeling and regression pipelines.

to_build.text: Implement a sparse variational Gaussian process layer wrapper tailored for learnable univariate edge functions in Kolmogorov-Arnold network topologies.
Develop analytic moment matching routines to propagate predictive uncertainty through deep compositional layers during regression training.
